title: heap-splay: KV shadow-index drift causing slab holes and GPU OOM cascade
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated environments reported sudden GPU OOM cascades correlated with large streaming chat workloads. Heap inspections show a recurring pattern we are calling 'heap-splay' where the KV index shadowing process races with session compaction leading to slab holes and persistent orphaned KV handles. Over time the slab fragmentation reduces usable contiguous GPU allocations and triggers OOMs for later requests. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and a runtime patch to address the leak/drift and add backpressure so hosts remain healthy.
impact: Several mid-market customers on Dedicated saw degraded throughput and 5xx errors for ~1-3 hours during peak traffic windows; hosted customers experienced intermittent 503s when a pool hit fragmentation-triggered OOMs. Business impact: live apps degraded; engineering incident escalations required manual node drains.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a Dedicated GPU pool with mixed-sequence-length chat workload
2) Run synthetic streaming workload that alternates many short prefix requests with occasional long-context generations (50-1024 tokens)
3) Enable KV index background compaction at default cadence
4) Observe memory growth in slab arenas, increased runtime_kv_orphan_handles_total, and intermittent allocator failure logs before OOMs
initial_mitigation_steps: 1) Temporarily throttle long-context jobs on affected pools via RateLimiter config
2) Force a graceful node drain in Dedicated pools to reclaim slab fragments
3) Deploy temporary KV reclamation cron on hosted control plane to run more frequent tombstone compaction
4) Add alert for runtime_kv_orphan_handles_total > 1000 per-node and runtime_gpu_free_bytes < 1GiB
root_cause_summary: A race between KV shadow-index sweeps and session-state compaction left index entries pointing to freed handles (soft-orphans). Orphaned handles keep tiny allocations alive and fragment arena bitmaps. The allocator's best-fit behavior exacerbates external fragmentation: small holes accumulate and the GPU allocator is unable to service a large contiguous request, producing OOM even though total free bytes appear sufficient. Additionally, the request router lacked a memory-aware backpressure signal, so high-concurrency bursts accelerated the failure.
proposed_fix: 1) Implement epoch-based reclamation in the KV shadow-index reconciler to ensure handles are only reclaimed after all readers complete. 2) Add an in-runtime slab coalescer that detects adjacent free spans and merges them asynchronously during low-load windows. 3) Introduce a GPU memory backpressure token to the router (soft-shed) that reduces concurrency for long-context generations when contiguous free space drops below threshold. 4) Add per-session soft-quotas and an async drain path to clear prefix/KV cache for idle sessions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs behind feature flags (kv.epoch_reclaim, allocator.coalesce, router.gpu_backpressure)
2) Canary to staging Dedicated pools (single region) for 24 hours with synthetic workloads
3) Expand canary to 10% of Hosted pools and 25% of Dedicated daytime traffic for 48 hours
4) Monitor memory fragmentation metrics and error rates, then progressive 100% rollout over 3 days if stable
5) If regressions detected, immediately flip feature flag off and trigger rollback automation
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch reclamation correctness and race conditions
Stress test harness using 'weave-writer' with mixed short/long sequences (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/testing-tools/tree/main/weave)
GPU perfbench runs on dedicated staging nodes with instrumented allocator traces
Long-duration soak (72h) at peak qps with artifacted heapdiff snapshots every 6 hours
Chaos test: concurrent KV index compaction and forced delayed reader completion to ensure reclamation safety
monitoring_queries: Alert: when runtime_kv_orphan_handles_total > 500 and runtime_gpu_free_bytes < 2GiB for 5m
postmortem_actions: Ship epoch-based reclamation and slab coalescer to stable with rollout notes
Update autoscaler to prefer smaller slab-preferred placements during high-frag windows
Add new quota metric and SLOs for contiguous allocation availability
Schedule a follow-up ticket to audit other compaction paths for similar races
